questions.q: How is Autonomous different from TeleOp?
questions.correct: It runs a fixed plan once, with no driver
wrong: It reads the gamepad the entire match
It only prints telemetry and never moves
It drives about twice as fast as TeleOp
questions.explain: TeleOp reads the gamepad forever; Autonomous runs a pre-written list of steps once, with no human input, then stops.

questions.q: What does @Autonomous do?
questions.correct: Marks the program to show in the autonomous slot
wrong: Makes the whole robot drive much faster
Reverses the two left drive motors for it
Charges the robot's battery before a match
questions.explain: @Autonomous is a label (annotation) marking the program as autonomous, so it appears in the autonomous list on the Driver Hub — like @TeleOp does for TeleOp.

questions.q: What is Pedro Pathing?
questions.correct: A library that steers the robot to exact spots
wrong: A sensor that measures the robot's ground speed
A motor that spins the odometry tracking wheels
A battery pack made for long autonomous runs
questions.explain: Pedro Pathing is a borrowed library of path-following math. You hand it a plan and it smoothly steers the robot to exact field positions.

questions.q: What is a .jar file?
questions.correct: A zip of code that someone else already wrote
wrong: A single line of code copied from a lesson
A sensor plugged into the Control Hub port
A battery used only during autonomous mode
questions.explain: A .jar is a bundle (zip) of someone's compiled code — a library. You import from it to use its classes, like Pedro's Follower.

questions.q: What does the Follower need to work?
questions.correct: A Localizer and a Drivetrain
wrong: A camera and a microphone
Two extra batteries and a fan
A gamepad held by the driver
questions.explain: The Follower needs a Localizer (where am I?) and a Drivetrain (how do I push the wheels?). It combines them to drive to a target pose.

questions.q: What does PinpointLocalizer answer?
questions.correct: Where am I on the field?
wrong: How do I push the wheels?
How fast should I shoot?
Which button was just pressed?
questions.explain: PinpointLocalizer wraps the Pinpoint sensor and answers "where am I?" The MecanumDrivetrainSubsystem answers "how do I push the wheels?"

questions.q: A Pose stores its heading in...
questions.correct: Radians
wrong: Degrees
Inches
Ticks
questions.explain: Pose heading is in radians, the unit the driving math prefers. You think in degrees, so wrap them with Math.toRadians(...).

questions.q: Why write Math.toRadians(90) in a Pose?
questions.correct: You think in degrees, but Pose wants radians
wrong: The robot drives faster measured in radians
Degrees are against the FTC competition rules
It resets the robot's heading back to zero
questions.explain: A Pose expects radians, but degrees are easier to reason about. Math.toRadians converts your degree value to the radians the Pose needs.

questions.q: What does follower.setStartingPose(startPose) do?
questions.correct: Tells the code exactly where the robot begins
wrong: Drives the robot to the very first waypoint
Spins the flywheel all the way up to speed
Prints the starting pose onto the telemetry
questions.explain: setStartingPose plants the robot's known starting spot. From then on, its tracked position is in field inches — so paths line up with reality.

questions.q: Why never use sleep() in autonomous?
questions.correct: It freezes the robot; use a pump-and-wait loop instead
wrong: It makes the robot drive a great deal faster
It is against the FTC competition rulebook
It drains the robot's battery far too quickly
questions.explain: sleep() freezes everything. Instead you loop, calling follower.update() and robot.update() many tiny times until the action reports it's done — never one big freeze.

questions.q: In the follow-and-wait loop, you must call...
questions.correct: follower.update() and robot.update() every pass
wrong: only follower.update(), never the robot
only robot.update(), never the follower
telemetry.update() and nothing else at all
questions.explain: Each loop you call follower.update() (drive one step) and robot.update() (advance mechanisms). Both run so driving and mechanisms make progress together.

questions.q: What tells you a path is still running?
questions.correct: follower.isBusy() returns true
wrong: gamepad1.a returns true
The battery voltage stays high
telemetry keeps printing lines
questions.explain: while (opModeIsActive() && follower.isBusy()) keeps pumping updates until the Follower reaches the target and isBusy() turns false — then the segment ends.

questions.q: A BezierLine is...
questions.correct: A straight path from one pose to the next
wrong: A spinning motion done in place
A single telemetry message line
A drive motor set into reverse
questions.explain: A BezierLine is a straight path between two poses. A PathChain bundles one (or more) up for the Follower to drive along.

questions.q: Why does SimpleAuto still build a Robot and call robot.update()?
questions.correct: So mechanisms stay alive and later actions can use them
wrong: Because Pedro Pathing can't drive unless the intake is running
To move the field's origin back to the robot before every path
Because robot.update() is what draws the path on the field
questions.explain: Autonomous builds the same Robot as TeleOp and keeps its scheduler running, so the next lesson can add actions like shooting with the subsystems you already wrote.

questions.q: Where is (0, 0) on the field?
questions.correct: The center of the field
wrong: The red alliance's starting corner
Wherever the robot was turned on
The front-left corner of the robot
questions.explain: Pose x and y are field inches measured from the origin at the center of the field. That's why the start pose must match where you place the robot.

questions.q: A pose of (12, -36, 0°) means the robot is...
questions.correct: 12 in toward +X, 36 in toward -Y (right), facing +X
wrong: 12 in to the left and 36 in forward, facing to the left
12 feet forward and 36 feet right, with no heading at all
Told to drive 12 in, then turn 36°, then stop facing 0°
questions.explain: x = 12 is 12 inches toward +X, y = -36 is 36 inches toward -Y (right, since +Y is left), and heading 0° faces +X.

questions.q: What does a PathChain do?
questions.correct: Strings BezierLines together into one path, in order
wrong: Picks the shortest line and skips all of the others
Drives every line at the same time, side by side
Saves the path into a file on the Control Hub
questions.explain: A PathChain joins straight BezierLines end to end, so the Follower drives start → pose 1 → pose 2 as one path.

questions.q: setLinearHeadingInterpolation(0°, 90°) on a line makes the robot...
questions.correct: Turn smoothly from 0° to 90° along the line
wrong: Spin to 90° first, then drive the whole line facing forward
Drive the line twice, once facing each of the two headings
Ignore both headings and keep facing 0° the entire time
questions.explain: Linear heading interpolation blends the heading from the start value to the end value as the robot travels the line.

questions.q: What does the simulator's Path Capture tool write for you?
questions.correct: The poses, the path chain and the follow-and-wait loop
wrong: Only a list of button presses and how long each one lasted
A new robot configuration file for the Driver Hub app
Shooting code that runs automatically at every saved pose
questions.explain: A captured auto has the same pieces as SimpleAuto: Pose lines, a PathChain of BezierLines, setStartingPose and the follow-and-wait loop. Path Capture just measures the poses for you.

questions.q: What is a dependency?
questions.correct: Code that now needs a library present to compile
wrong: A battery the whole robot depends on
A button the driver is required to hold
A tracking wheel that must stay dead
questions.explain: Once you import from a library, your code depends on that library being present to build. That's a dependency — remove the library and it won't compile.
